title: Can You See the Wall?
passage: For centuries, people believed that the Great Wall of China could be seen from the Moon. The idea appeared in books, classrooms, and even quiz shows. It sounded amazing—but it is not true.

Astronauts who have traveled to the Moon report that no human-made structures are visible from that distance. Even from a much lower orbit, the Great Wall is very hard to see because it is narrow and its color is similar to the land around it. Highways and airports, which are wider and brighter, are actually easier to spot.
Why did the myth last so long? Part of the reason is that it was repeated so often that people stopped questioning it. The story reminds us that even popular "facts" deserve a second look.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To describe how the Great Wall was built
To correct a widely held but mistaken belief
To encourage readers to become astronauts
To compare China's highways with its airports
questions.explain: 作者要糾正「從月球看得到長城」這個流傳很廣的錯誤說法。

questions.q: What have people who flew to the Moon said?
options: They could clearly see the Great Wall.
Nothing built by humans can be made out from there.
Only airports can be seen from there.
The Earth looked completely dark.
questions.explain: 第二段：登月的太空人表示，從那麼遠的地方看不到任何人造建築。

questions.q: Why is the Wall difficult to notice even from closer to Earth?
options: It is usually covered by snow.
It is too thin and matches the colors of its surroundings.
Most of it was destroyed long ago.
It is hidden under trees.
questions.explain: 第二段：長城很窄，顏色又和周圍的土地相近。

questions.q: In paragraph 2, "spot" is closest in meaning to ____.
options: clean
notice
build
avoid
questions.explain: spot 在這裡當動詞，意思是「看見、發現」，和 notice 相同。

questions.q: What habit does the writer hope readers will develop?
options: Traveling to famous places
Checking whether well-known claims are really true
Watching more quiz shows
Memorizing facts about China
questions.explain: 最後一句：就算是大家都相信的「事實」也值得再查證。
